record_contract.forms: A compact representation of the language's ordinary nominal-number inventory or marking strategy. It may name categories such as singular/dual/plural or explicitly say that noun number is commonly unmarked.
record_contract.own_grammar_blurb: One short learner-facing explanation written in the language itself describing how that language ordinarily handles grammatical number. It must not assume that every language has obligatory singular/plural noun inflection.
record_contract.source_refs: Research references supporting the language-specific claim when available. WALS 33A/34A provide the shared typological baseline; full target-language records add target-specific grammar references where practical.
record_contract.review_state: machine_translated records are candidates and must remain visibly below human-reviewed trust levels.

research_notes: Grammatical number and CLDR plural categories are different systems; this catalog is about linguistic number marking and agreement, not localization plural-selection rules.
Absence of obligatory noun plural marking does not mean a language cannot express plural meaning.

The same language may use different strategies by animacy, definiteness, noun class, numeral construction, register, or dialect. Blurbs intentionally describe the broad learner-facing pattern rather than pretend to be exhaustive grammars.
